blinding_guess.why: The first rclpy subscription on a topic is QoS-matched to the publishers discovered at subscribe time (subscribers.py:112-133: default RELIABLE/VOLATILE depth 10, switched to TRANSIENT_LOCAL and/or BEST_EFFORT if any existing publisher uses them), and the tree carries launch tests for exactly those two cases (best_effort_publisher.test.py, transient_local_publisher.test.py, both registered in rosbridge_server/CMakeLists.txt:29-30), so the common single-client path looks sound at this revision. Two weak spots remain in the consumed-topic path: (a) publishers that appear after the subscription are not matched (acknowledged in the code comment at subscribers.py:119-125); (b) when a second client subscribes to an already-subscribed topic, MultiSubscriber.subscribe creates an extra rclpy subscription with the plain depth argument 10 (subscribers.py:173-175), i.e. rclpy's default RELIABLE/VOLATILE profile rather than the matched qos, so against a BEST_EFFORT publisher that second client's first message never arrives and its callback is never moved into self.subscriptions; the multi-client test (multiple_subscribers.test.py) exists in the tree but is not registered in CMakeLists.txt. Whether the paired scenario exercises the sound single-client path or one of these two paths cannot be determined from the packet, so I cannot tell.

notes: rosbridge_server does not name /my_topic anywhere; it subscribes to whatever topic a WebSocket client requests via the rosbridge protocol subscribe op (subscribe.py:235-283; documented at snapshot:ROSBRIDGE_PROTOCOL.md:386-429), so the consumed element is neither in declares/not_declared (it is not provided) nor in references (name supplied at run time). The actual rclpy subscription lives in the exec dependency rosbridge_library (same repository, version 1.1.0 at snapshot:rosbridge_library/package.xml:4), which this recon treats as the code path of rosbridge_server's subscription. Static facts about that subscription: message type = client 'type' field or inferred from the graph, TypeConflictException if the two disagree (subscribers.py:100-102); history depth 10; reliability and durability are selected at run time by the rule quoted under ports[0].qos, so both are recorded as null; deadline is never set; the raw flag is set when the client asks for compression 'cbor-raw' (subscribe.py:130). Frame and units are null because the message type is unknown. throttle_rate/queue_length/fragment_size/compression are per-client delivery modifiers, not ROS rates, hence rate_hz and min_rate_hz are null. exclusive lists the TCP listening port (parameter 'port', default 9090; tests use port 0 for an ephemeral port at snapshot:rosbridge_server/test/websocket/common.py:52). perm_grants: the three glob parameters are fnmatch allowlists applied to client subscribe/unsubscribe/publish/advertise/service/param operations; an empty value (the default) disables the check; when services_glob is non-empty '/rosapi/*' is appended; check_origin always returns True (websocket_handler.py:233-234), so any WebSocket origin is accepted. The package also provides topics not in the packet: client_count (std_msgs/Int32, TRANSIENT_LOCAL, created twice: rosbridge_websocket.py:119-127 depth 10 and client_mananger.py:44-51 depth 1) and connected_clients (rosbridge_msgs/ConnectedClients, TRANSIENT_LOCAL depth 1, client_mananger.py:54-56). Advertised publishers are unregistered lazily after unregister_timeout (default 10.0 s, publishers.py:202, 276), which is a publish-side mechanism and not part of the subscription path. No dependency definition files were fetched because no message type is fixed for this element.
